# Errors, readiness and health

Error text a plugin writes is fixed English plus at most a number, and may name what the config holds (a device's local id, a config key). It never holds a secret, a URL, or what the device sent: map the device's codes to sentences of your own. The hub shows it to people and writes it to the audit log.

## `DeviceError`

Why a device did not do what it was asked, or could not be read.

Every helper in this crate returns it, and so does every driver. Its text is fixed, or is device-supplied text made safe, and never comes from the HTTP client, whose messages can include a URL.

Returned by `Driver::command`, `Driver::read_state` and the other driver calls, and by every socket helper in `swifty_plugin_api::net`, so `?` passes a helper's error straight on.

| Variant | Shown as | Silence | What the hub does | JSON |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Timeout` | `no reply from the device` | yes | Silence: the device may not have heard. An idempotent action is sent once more within its timeout; any other action never is. The run ends `no_response`. While the hub reads back for confirmation, it keeps reading. | `"Timeout"` |
| `Unreachable` | `device unreachable: the connection failed` | yes | Silence, as `Timeout`. | `{"Unreachable":"the connection failed"}` |
| `Rejected` | `device refused: the device sent an unreadable reply` | no | The device answered and said no, or answered with nonsense. The run ends `failed` with this text. During read-back it ends the run `failed` too, unless the operation takes the device away (a host shutdown). | `{"Rejected":"the device sent an unreadable reply"}` |
| `Disabled` | `This device cannot do that.` | no | The driver will not do this: the device is not one of this instance's, or cannot do it. The run ends `failed`. Anything the driver refuses this way should also be refused by `Plugin::refusal`, so that dry-run says the same (conformance check 5). | `{"Disabled":"This device cannot do that."}` |

`DeviceError::unsupported()` is `{"Disabled":"This device cannot do that."}`: the answer for something this device cannot do at all.

## `PluginError`

Why an instance could not be built. Shown on the plugin page. Fixed text, never a secret.

Returned by `Plugin::connect`. Example: `The secret token is not set.`

`Secrets::require(slot)` returns one when a slot is empty, naming the slot and nothing else. The hub disables that one instance with the text and keeps the others running.

## `ConfigProblem`

What is wrong with a config document: the field and a sentence.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `String` | The key of the field, or a dotted path to it. |
| `message` | `String` | What is wrong with it, as one sentence. |

Shown as `devices[0].address: must be an IP address`. JSON: `{"field":"devices[0].address","message":"must be an IP address"}`

Returned by `Plugin::validate` and `Plugin::migrate`. Name the field (a dotted path for a row, `devices[0].address`), and say what is wrong in a sentence. Conformance check 2 looks for the key in the field or the message.

## `Readiness`

Whether an instance can work.

| Variant | Meaning | What the hub does | JSON |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Ready` | It can. | The instance is loaded: in dry-run as a stand-in, when live through `Plugin::connect`. | `{"status":"ready"}` |
| `NeedsSetup` | Configured but not usable yet: not paired, a credential is missing. Its devices are listed, disabled, with this reason. | Its devices are listed, disabled, with this reason, and `connect` is not called. The app offers the setup. | `{"status":"needs_setup","reason":"The hub is not paired yet. Run the setup and press its button."}` |
| `Disabled` | Cannot work with this config. Same listing. | The same listing, with this reason. Nothing is called until the config changes. | `{"status":"disabled","reason":"The configuration is not valid: address: must be an IP address."}` |

Returned by the pure `Plugin::readiness`, from the config and the slots that hold a value. Conformance checks 4 to 12 need `Ready` for the fixture.

## `Health`

How an instance's connection to its devices is doing.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `HealthStatus` | The verdict. |
| `detail` | `Option<String>` | One sentence on why, when there is one. |

| Status | Meaning | Example JSON |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | Everything answers. | `{"status":"ok","detail":null}` |
| `degraded` | Some of it answers. | `{"status":"degraded","detail":"2 of 3 blinds answer."}` |
| `down` | Nothing answers. | `{"status":"down","detail":"The hub refused the access token."}` |
| `unknown` | Not known yet. | `{"status":"unknown","detail":null}` |

Returned by `Driver::health`, which the hub calls now and then while live. Its default is `unknown`. Keep it to one cheap read; never change anything.
